options.text: The current will keep increasing without limit, because it is larger in each successive row.
options.why: Believes an increasing sequence has no upper limit.

options.text: The current is increasing at a constant rate, because it rises by the same amount in each interval.
options.why: Reads the table as linear although the increases get smaller.

options.text: The current is approaching a final value, because each equal time interval closes the same fraction of the remaining gap to that value.
options.why: The remaining gap to $120\text{ mA}$ shrinks by a constant factor each interval, as for $I=I_\infty(1-e^{-t/\tau})$.

options.text: The current rises instantly to its final value, because the inductor has no effect on the circuit.
options.why: Ignores that an inductor opposes the change in current.

ap_physics_c_electricity_and_magnetism-m.stem: Loop 1 has radius $4\text{ cm}$ and loop 2 has radius $12\text{ cm}$. Each lies perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field; the field at loop 1 changes at $1\text{ T/s}$ and the field at loop 2 changes at $0.5\text{ T/s}$. What is the ratio of the emf induced in loop 2 to that induced in loop 1?

options.why: $\varepsilon_2/\varepsilon_1=(r_2/r_1)^2(\text{rate}_2/\text{rate}_1)=4.50$.
Compares the radii only, $r_2/r_1$.
Compares the rates only.
Uses $r^2/(dB/dt)$.

ap_physics_c_electricity_and_magnetism-m.stem: A long solenoid has inductance $L$. A second long solenoid has $3$ times as many turns, is $4$ times as long and has $2$ times the cross-sectional area. What is the inductance of the second solenoid?

options.why: Divides by the area instead of multiplying, $N^2/(A\ell)$.
Uses $N$ instead of $N^2$.
Ignores the area factor.
$L\propto N^2A/\ell$, so the new inductance is $3^2\cdot2/4\,L=4.50L$.

ap_physics_c_electricity_and_magnetism-m.stem: A coil rotating in a uniform magnetic field has a maximum induced emf $\varepsilon_{max}$. The rotation rate is multiplied by $3$, the number of turns is multiplied by $3$ and the field is multiplied by $4$, with the area unchanged. What is the new maximum emf?

options.text: $2.25\varepsilon_{max}$
options.why: Divides by the field factor.

options.text: $10.0\varepsilon_{max}$
options.why: Adds the three factors.

options.text: $36.0\varepsilon_{max}$
options.why: $\varepsilon_{max}\propto N B\omega$, so the new value is $3\cdot3\cdot4\,\varepsilon_{max}=36.0\varepsilon_{max}$.

options.text: $12.0\varepsilon_{max}$
options.why: Ignores the number of turns.
